tasks.gr8-visual-arts-t4: Topic: Visual Arts. Cover portfolio selection, exhibition planning, finishing techniques, and reflection. Ask Grade 8 learners to choose strong portfolio pieces, justify display decisions, and evaluate artwork quality using appropriate art terms.
tasks.gr8-music-t4: Topic: Music. Cover performance revision, genre comparison, aural recall, and stage etiquette. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify genre features, respond to aural prompts, and select rehearsal and etiquette choices that strengthen final performances.
tasks.gr8-drama-t4: Topic: Drama. Cover scripted performance, rehearsal discipline, audience etiquette, and evaluation. Ask Grade 8 learners to choose rehearsal strategies, identify cue and performance quality indicators, and evaluate dramatic techniques with evidence.
tasks.gr8-dance-t4: Topic: Dance. Cover final routines, timing, expression, appreciation, and careers awareness. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify performance-quality markers, apply safe and expressive movement choices, and recognise dance-related roles in school and community contexts.
tasks.gr8-ca-six-eight-d-major-t4: Topic: 6/8, D major, tempo and articulation. Cover the time signature 6/8 (six quavers in a bar felt as two beats of three, a dotted crotchet each), the D major scale (two sharps, F sharp and C sharp), the tempo words moderato, presto, ritardando and a tempo, the articulation words legato and staccato, and writing an impression of music you listened to (instruments, tempo, dynamics, mood). Ask Grade 8 learners to count quavers and beats, name the sharps in D major and match the terms to their meanings.
tasks.gr8-ca-dialogue-storytelling-t4: Topic: Dialogues, dramatised prose and indigenous storytelling. Cover dialogue (text analysis, vocal and physical characterisation, use of space, staying in character, status and relationships), dramatised prose from South African authors (narrator and characters, change of role), indigenous storytelling (legends, fairy tales, ntsomi, narrative technique, songs, idiophones, sound effects) and the interpretation tools pause, pitch, pace, projection, intonation and tone. Do not quote any real text. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify these terms and choose the right technique.
tasks.gr8-ca-media-t4: Topic: Drama in the media. Cover forms of media (film, television, radio, documentaries, the internet), drama elements identified in a media form (what, who, where, when, tension, structure), how radio uses voices, sound effects and music and film uses a camera, acting and editing, and responding to a media drama using drama terms with a reason. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify media forms and drama elements and to choose a good response.
tasks.gr8-ca-tone-texture-t4: Topic: Tone and texture: crumpled fabric, oil pastel and tempera. Cover drawing crumpled fabric with 2B or 3B pencils on A3 paper (light on the folds, dark in the creases, mark-making for texture), the design principles balance, proportion, harmony, rhythm, emphasis and contrast, themed artwork with oil pastel and tempera (plan, sketches, layering and blending, opaque paint), and talking about artworks in the wider world (look, name, question, reflect). Do not name real artists or artworks. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify tone, principles and the steps of the process.
tasks.gr8-ca-scraperboard-t4: Topic: Scraperboard etching. Cover the wax and ink method on stiff board about 20 x 20 cm (white wax crayon, black ink or tempera with a little dishwashing liquid, dry completely, scratch with a sharp tool), shape, line, tone and texture in scratched drawing (more scratching makes a lighter tone), contrast, proportion and emphasis in a still life, and safe use of sharp tools (scratch away from the body, protect the table, never point a tool at a person, put tools away). Ask Grade 8 learners to order the steps, explain tone and choose safe practice.
tasks.gr8-ca-gestures-movement-t4: Topic: Gestures and the movement sentence. Cover gestures, literal gestures (everyday actions as they look), changing gestures from literal to abstract (size, speed, body part, level, direction, repetition), the movement sentence as gestures joined with counts (for example 4 gestures of 2 counts = 8 counts), and composing a sequence about an idea, mood or thought with rehearsal, revision and reflection. Ask Grade 8 learners to tell literal from abstract gestures, count a sentence and order the steps of composing.
